change.detail: severely wounded leading the charge; Lieutenant-Colonel Gaillard conducted the regiment afterwards

quote: Col. John D. Kennedy, of the Second South Carolina Regiment, was severely wounded while gallantly leading his command to the charge. Lieutenant-Colonel [F. ] Gaillard conducted the regiment through its subsequent operations.
note: Kershaw's report.

change.detail: fallen when Kershaw reached the regiment; Major Gist in command

quote: Its gallant and accomplished commander had just fallen when I reached it, and it was under the command of Major [William M.] Gist.
note: Kershaw's report speaks of the Fifteenth South Carolina; it names Colonel De Saussure beside it in the sentence before.

Kershaw's report names the battalion by its original commander's name (James' battalion) and gives it as the Third Battalion South Carolina Infantry in the casualty paragraph; the table prints it as the 3d South Carolina battalion, Lieut. Col. W. G. Rice.

quote: as was also Maj. D. B. Miller, James' battalion [Third Battalion South Carolina Infantry]
Major [D. McD.] McLeod, of the Eighth South Carolina Regiment, a gallant and estimable ofiicer, was mortally wounded.
I changed the direction of the right wing of the regiment, under Lieutenant-Colonel [Elbert] Bland, to meet the attack
note: The same report says Bland was severely wounded while commanding the right wing.

quote: I changed the direction of the Seventh Regiment (Colonel Aiken) and the Third (Major [R. C] Maflfett) to the left
note: Kershaw's report. The name is printed Maflfett in the OCR; Maffett in the table and in the officer's own report.

change.detail: arrived on the afternoon of the 3d and assumed command in person

quote: Colonel [J. D.] Nance arrived late in the afternoon of the 3d, and assumed command in person.
note: Major Maffett's report; Nance's own report (R434) agrees.

change.detail: while leading his brigade in the assault

quote: Brigadier-General Barksdale was mortally wounded in the attack on the evening of the 2d, while bravely leading his brigade in the assault.
note: Longstreet's report. The organization table lists Brig. Gen. William Barksdale first and Col. B. G. Humphreys second; the OCR of that block is too damaged to match a quote.

quote: Humphreys succeeded to the command of the now famous brigade, consisting of the Thirteenth, Seventeenth, Eighteenth and, Twenty- first regiments of Mississippi infantry.
note: Confederate Military History (1899) says Humphreys succeeded Barksdale; it dates the event to the first day, which the reports place on 2 July. The table (scan) prints Col. B. G. Humphreys under Barksdale's name; the OCR cannot be matched.

change.detail: severely wounded and since died of his wounds (report of 27 July)

quote: General Barksdale mortally wounded, and General Semmes severely wounded, and since died of his wounds
note: Longstreet's report.

quote: with General Wofford, the enemy made a hasty retreat
note: Longstreet's report names General Wofford commanding with the division in the retreat; the table prints Brig. Gen. W. T. Wofford (the OCR of that line cannot be matched).

value.detail: after being sent to Virginia the battalion was assigned to Wofford brigade; after Gettysburg it accompanied Longstreet to Georgia

quote: This battalion after being sent to Virginia was assigned to Wofford's brigade. After Gettysburg it accompanied Longstreet to Georgia
note: Confederate Military History (1899): the battalion was in Wofford brigade, and went with Longstreet after Gettysburg, so it was with the brigade at the battle. The organization table of the Official Records does not list it.

quote: The Third battalion Georgia infantry, sharpshooters, was organized with the following field officers: Lieut. - Col. L. N. Hutchins, Maj. H. H. Smith
note: The volume names the battalion's field officers at organization (1862); it does not say who commanded in July 1863.
